articles.title: El fallo informático de la FIA que detuvo la Fórmula 1 en Malasia y provocó el caos en la salida
articles.text:
Un fallo informático en el software de la Federación Internacional del Automóvil (FIA) dejó sin potencia a varios monoplazas durante la vuelta de formación en Sepang, Malasia, y obligó a detener el inicio de la carrera. La incidencia afectó a unidades de potencia de distintos fabricantes bajo lluvia y provocó una bandera roja antes de la salida.
El problema expuso una vulnerabilidad en la nueva generación de motores de Fórmula 1, cuya potencia combina sistemas de combustión e híbridos. La FIA tuvo que distribuir una actualización urgente a todos los equipos para recuperar el funcionamiento de los coches, tras una demora que superó una hora y media desde el horario previsto.
La vuelta de formación reveló el fallo
La situación comenzó bajo un fuerte aguacero, cuando los monoplazas salieron a realizar la vuelta de formación. Varios motores, incluidos los de Lewis Hamilton, Oliver Bearman y Valtteri Bottas, mostraron problemas y amenazaron con detenerse.
Según explicó la FIA, el fallo apareció por una combinación de baja velocidad, escaso agarre y pista mojada. Algunos coches circularon tan despacio detrás de Max Verstappen que estuvieron cerca de detenerse por completo, lo que activó un error en el sistema que administra la potencia eléctrica.
La categoría utiliza un software para regular la energía disponible según las condiciones de la pista. En lluvia, el sistema limita la potencia eléctrica a 250 kW, frente a los 350 kW habilitados en otras situaciones, como los momentos de adelantamiento.
El error impidió que la potencia volviera a entrar en varios coches. Al no poder recuperar aceleración de forma normal, la dirección de carrera mostró la bandera roja y ordenó una nueva neutralización antes de la salida.
La FIA envió una actualización en plena emergencia
La interrupción permitió a los técnicos identificar el origen del problema. La FIA eliminó el límite de energía mediante una actualización de software que se distribuyó entre los equipos, quienes tuvieron que instalarla en sus monoplazas antes de reanudar el procedimiento.
Nikolas Tombazis, responsable técnico de monoplazas de la FIA, explicó que el trabajo se realizó bajo presión. El responsable técnico sostuvo que el envío de la actualización y su instalación tomaron unos 20 minutos. Sin embargo, la carrera acumuló una demora mayor por el aguacero previo, la reorganización de la parrilla y el nuevo procedimiento de salida.
La FIA restableció la parrilla original tras la bandera roja, aunque no ofreció una explicación inmediata. El organismo publicó un comunicado tres horas después, en el que confirmó que el problema no había sido detectado en las pruebas ni durante las vueltas previas a la formación.
La falta de rodaje en lluvia complicó la detección
Tombazis reconoció que la nueva motorización no había tenido suficientes pruebas en condiciones de mojado. La temporada de 2026 no registró sesiones de pista con lluvia durante los grandes premios y el modo específico para esas circunstancias solo se utilizó de forma limitada en una prueba de neumáticos de Red Bull en Suzuka.
El reglamento actual incrementó el peso de la parte eléctrica en las unidades de potencia. Según la información difundida, los motores tienen cerca de un 47% de potencia eléctrica, una proporción que exige controles específicos para evitar una entrega excesiva de energía sobre asfalto mojado.
“El software se desarrolla por la FIA en colaboración con los equipos, con el suministrador de las centralitas y con los fabricantes de motores. No se había anticipado este problema antes, tenemos que hacerlo mejor”, admitió Tombazis.
La FIA anunció un análisis junto con los equipos y los fabricantes Mercedes, Ferrari, RB Ford, Audi y Honda. El objetivo será revisar por qué la combinación de baja velocidad y lluvia activó un fallo que no había aparecido en las simulaciones ni en las pruebas disponibles.
Los pilotos cuestionaron la complejidad del reglamento
La demora provocó críticas de varios pilotos. Carlos Sainz consideró que era previsible que surgiera una situación similar debido a la complejidad de los motores actuales y a la dependencia del software para controlar la energía eléctrica.
“Era cuestión de tiempo que pasara una cosa así”, afirmó el piloto español. Sainz cuestionó la decisión reglamentaria tomada años atrás y sostuvo que la Fórmula 1 debe revisar cómo llegó a depender de cambios de mapas y controles desde dirección de carrera para gestionar la potencia entre condiciones secas y mojadas.
Checo Pérez calificó el episodio de “inaceptable”, mientras que Lando Norris lo describió como “simplemente horrible”. George Russell lamentó el efecto para el público, tras una jornada marcada por la espera, la bandera roja y las vueltas detrás del coche de seguridad.
Fernando Alonso, que terminó octavo con Aston Martin, utilizó la ironía: “Este año he tenido un 50% de abandonos, pero nunca han parado la carrera por nuestra culpa”.
El incidente de Sepang dejó una señal para la FIA antes de las próximas carreras con lluvia: la nueva arquitectura híbrida requiere más pruebas para evitar que una actualización urgente vuelva a decidir el inicio de un Gran Premio.

articles.title: Insta360 Luna Ultra : la nouvelle caméra de poche qui fait trembler DJI avec son double objectif Leica
articles.text:
Après des années de règne sans partage de DJI sur le segment des caméras de poche stabilisées, Insta360 montre ses muscles avec la Luna Ultra. Conçue avec Leica, elle mise sur un double objectif, un écran Oled détachable, qui fait aussi office de télécommande, et une fiche technique alléchante.
DJI a longtemps régné en maître sur le marché naissant des mini-caméras à nacelle stabilisée avec sa série Osmo Pocket. L'arrivée de la gamme Insta360 Luna vient rebattre les cartes. La marque chinoise, plus connue pour ses caméras 360° et ses action-cams, s'attaque frontalement à ce segment avec un produit qui ne fait pas dans la demi-mesure. La Luna Ultra embarque un double bloc optique conçu avec Leica, un capteur principal de 1 pouce associé à un objectif 20 mm (équivalent plein format) f/1,8, épaulé par un téléobjectif 60 mm f/2 monté sur un capteur 1/1,3 pouce.
Autre singularité : l'écran tactile Oled de 2 pouces se détache entièrement du corps de la caméra pour se transformer en télécommande à retour vidéo avec une portée annoncée d'une vingtaine de mètres. Une première dans le segment des caméras de poche, qui change concrètement la manière de cadrer certains plans. Le tout est piloté par une triple puce, dont un processeur IA gravé en 4 nm pour épauler la stabilisation, le suivi du sujet, la mise au point et le traitement en basse lumière.
L'Insta360 Luna Ultra est commercialisée en deux coloris, noir cosmique et blanc stellaire, et se décline en plusieurs configurations. Le pack standard, facturé 729 €, comprend la caméra, une bonnette anti-vent, une poignée filetée au standard 1/4 de pouce, un câble USB-C, une dragonne et une housse de protection.
Pour les créateurs de contenus les plus exigeants, Insta360 propose un pack créateur à 929 € (objet de ce test). Celui-ci ajoute une lentille grand-angle magnétique élargissant le champ de vision à 108°, une poignée avec batterie supplémentaire (le fameux power grip), une pochette de transport et, surtout, un émetteur Mic Pro, le micro sans fil de la marque doté d'un écran e-ink personnalisable.
Entre les deux, Insta360 propose aussi un pack endurance (831 €), un pack essentiel (831 € également avec un filtre Black Mist), un pack vlog (858 € avec sangle et micro Mic Air) et un pack POV (837 €) avec un accessoire de suivi de tête.
Premier contact, première bonne surprise : la Luna Ultra est plus compacte qu'elle n'y paraît sur les photos. Son format ressemble très fortement à celui de sa concurrente, avec cette nacelle motorisée qui dépasse en partie haute et les deux objectifs Leica bien visibles côte à côte. Comparée à la Pocket 4P de DJI, le poids est quasi identique (233 g pour la Luna Ultra, 230 g pour la Pocket 4P).
La Luna Ultra demeure très maniable, mais le gabarit est différent. Elle est plus longue (169,9 mm contre 159,5 mm) et plus épaisse (38,5 mm contre 33,5 mm), tandis que la Pocket 4P est plus large (63,3 mm contre 52,4 mm). La Luna Ultra se distingue aussi par son écran Oled détachable, quand celui de la Pocket 4P reste fixé à demeure.
Le fabricant fournit une mini-poignée qui se fixe sous la base : elle améliore sensiblement la prise en main et ajoute un filetage 1/4 de pouce standard, ainsi qu'un minuscule trépied repliable, pratique pour poser l'appareil sur une table. Le pack créateur inclut en plus le power grip, une version rallongée de cette poignée intégrant une batterie additionnelle — l'ensemble accompagne alors la caméra sur une bonne journée de tournage sans recharge.
La finition, en tout cas sur notre modèle noir cosmique, ne souffre d'aucune critique. Le plastique dur employé donne une impression de solidité bienvenue, loin d'un simple gadget, et le boîtier (fourni) enveloppe entièrement la nacelle pour la protéger des chocs. On regrette en revanche que la Luna Ultra ne soit pas taillée pour l'aventure comme peuvent l'être les action-cams de la marque. Elle n'affiche aucune certification officielle d'étanchéité, un point sur lequel nous revenons plus loin.
Deux boutons orange, situés à la base de la caméra, permettent de libérer l'écran d'une simple pression. Une fois séparé, il embarque deux touches personnalisables, un mini-joystick cliquable commandant la nacelle, une glissière de zoom et un déclencheur, le tout alimenté par sa propre batterie.
Sur le terrain, l'intérêt saute aux yeux dès la première prise de vue en solo : poser la caméra au ras du sol, en contre-plongée, pour un plan qui aurait autrement nécessité de se contorsionner pour cadrer, puis piloter le tout à distance, debout, écran en main. C'est simple, redoutablement pratique, et personne d'autre ne le propose encore sur ce type de produit.
Un bémol tout de même : pour un cadrage millimétré, la définition de l'écran atteint vite ses limites. Idem, l’opération de détachement, répétée trop souvent, pourrait à terme fragiliser le connecteur.
L'apport de Leica dans le co-développement de la Luna Ultra porte notamment sur les deux objectifs Summicron fixés à sa tête : un grand-angle équivalent 20 mm ouvert à f/1,8, placé devant un capteur 1 pouce d'environ 50 Mpx, et un téléobjectif équivalent 60 mm f/2 adossé à un capteur 1/1,3 pouce de 9 Mpx. Le tout est stabilisé par une nacelle trois axes couplée à une stabilisation électronique.
La Luna Ultra possède aussi un capteur dédié à la température de couleur, niché entre les deux optiques. Ce duo 20 mm/60 mm permet de zoomer jusqu'à 6x, puis 15x grâce à l'IA, comme nous le communique Insta360. Dans les faits, les différents facteurs de zoom intermédiaires depuis les deux objectifs sont obtenus en recadrant dans le fichier DNG, comme nous avons pu le vérifier en comparant le raw et le jpeg d'un même fichier directement produit par la Luna Ultra. La notion de “zoom sans perte” annoncée par Insta360 n'est donc qu'un artifice marketing trompeur.
La lecture des fichiers met toutefois en évidence la qualité de traitement des algorithmes et de l'IA d'Insta360 jusqu'au facteur 6x. Au-delà, la qualité des images se dégrade de manière visible jusqu'à 15x. Le téléobjectif est le véritable atout de la Luna Ultra, dont l'efficacité du traitement des différents facteurs de zoom permet de préserver le piqué des images. Le zoom 6x reste exploitable, mais sa limite d'utilisation raisonnable reste calée à 3x pour conserver une qualité d'image optimale.
La Luna Ultra permet de travailler au format vertical. Une fois encore, l'utilisation des formats raw et jpeg nous a permis de voir comment la petite caméra de poche procédait, avec à chaque fois la production d'une image carrée de 6144 x 6144 pixels (quel que soit le facteur de zoom), redimensionnée puis traitée au format 3456 x 6144 pixels par les algorithmes de traitement internes. L'avantage du raw, en dehors de son potentiel en matière de postproduction, est surtout de posséder et conserver un original au format carré aux dimensions plus généreuses.
Images réalisées l'Insta360 Luna Ultra
Le mode photo standard de la Luna Pro capture des clichés de 9 Mpx, suffisants pour un partage rapide sur les réseaux, tandis que le mode UltraPhoto grimpe jusqu'à 37 Mpx et autorise l'enregistrement en RAW pour qui souhaite retoucher ses images en postproduction. Le rendu d'image par défaut est lumineux, un brin saturé, riche en détails et volontiers flatteur en utilisation avec les profils Leica (Natural, Vivid et Chrome). Insta360 annonce 14 stops de plage dynamique et une sensibilité de 100 à 6 400 ISO.
Au laboratoire des Numériques, la lecture des fichiers de test met en avant l'efficacité des algorithmes, avec une bonne maîtrise du bruit et un lissage raisonnable dès que l'on monte en sensibilité. En basse lumière, l'équilibre entre hautes et basses lumières reste bien géré avec du détail dans les ombres jusqu'à 400 ISO et, là encore, un lissage contenu. À partir de 800 ISO et jusqu'à 1600 ISO, le lissage est plus musclé et nous observons cette fois une perte de détails dans toutes les parties sombres de l'image.
Le terrain vidéo est sans conteste le point fort de la Luna Ultra. La caméra grimpe jusqu'en 8K à 30 images par seconde (i/s), propose de la 4K jusqu'à 120 i/s pour les ralentis et de la Full HD à 240 i/s. Le tout profite d'un encodage H.265 avec des débits pouvant atteindre 120 Mb/s. Insta360 ajoute à cela le support du Dolby Vision et d'un profil I-Log 10 bits capturant jusqu'à 14 stops de dynamique : une aubaine pour les vidéastes qui souhaitent conserver une matière riche à étalonner en postproduction. Les plus pointilleux apprécieront aussi la compatibilité avec le standard colorimétrique ACES, prisé du monde du cinéma, ainsi que la présence d'un timecode, même si celui-ci se limite en réalité à une simple synchronisation sur l'heure du jour.
Le format 8K à 30 i/s impressionne par son niveau de détail, mais ne sera pas forcément indispensable à tout le monde. La plupart de nos prises de vue au format 4K ont offert un rendu excellent en plein jour avec des couleurs chaudes et un contraste marqué. Le point fort de la Luna Ultra reste son second objectif.
Le passage entre les deux capteurs s'opère via la glissière de zoom située sous l'écran. Une poussée rapide fait passer d'un coup de 1x à 3x, tandis qu'un maintien permet un zoom progressif dont la vitesse est réglable dans les paramètres. Le zoom optique grimpe ainsi jusqu'à 3x, puis 6x sans perte grâce au recadrage dans le capteur 8K, avant de basculer sur un traitement numérique assisté par IA jusqu'à 15x depuis la dernière mise à jour. La dégradation de l'image devient sensible, sans pour autant la rendre inexploitable dans de bonnes conditions de lumière.
L'autofocus reste le principal point noir observé sur la Luna Ultra. Efficace au grand-angle, il est à la peine sur les petits sujets et a tendance à décrocher lors des transitions de zoom. Le suivi de sujet, en revanche, tient toutes ses promesses. Baptisé Deep Track 5.0, il reprend le savoir-faire des caméras 360° de la marque et s'accroche à son sujet avec une belle constance, y compris derrière des obstacles ponctuels comme un arbre ou un poteau. Ses différents modes (suivi automatique, avec zoom actif, cadrage de groupe) se montrent tous convaincants, en particulier le zoom actif qui ajuste seul la focale pour garder un cadrage constant à mesure que l'on s'approche ou s'éloigne du sujet.
Côté basse lumière, la caméra bascule automatiquement vers un mode dédié baptisé PureVideo, plafonné en 4K/60 i/s et incompatible avec le Dolby Vision et le profil I-Log. Le résultat surprend par sa qualité avec un bruit numérique efficacement contenu. Les scènes de rue nocturnes restent bien détaillées, loin de la bouillie de pixels qu'on pourrait redouter sur un capteur de cette taille. Nous sommes certes loin d'un capteur plein format, mais pour une caméra de poche, la qualité est étonnante. Attention aussi aux cadences légèrement fractionnaires (29,97, 59,94, 60,2, 60,4 i/s…) relevées dans ce mode, peu appréciées des professionnels en postproduction.
Concernant l'audio, la Luna Ultra embarque quatre microphones, dont un logé dans l'écran détachable. Le rendu se révèle tout à fait correct en intérieur ou en extérieur calme, mais la protection anti-vent montre vite ses limites dès que les conditions se corsent. D'où l'intérêt du Mic Pro fourni dans le pack créateur : directement compatible sans récepteur additionnel, il capture un son nettement plus propre grâce à son enregistrement interne en 32 bits flottant. Dommage que la caméra ne reconnaisse que les micros sans fil de la marque. Nos essais avec un micro tiers en Bluetooth se sont soldés par un échec pur et simple, la caméra ne détectant même pas l'appareil.
Insta360 n'annonce aucune certification officielle concernant l'étanchéité. Contrairement aux action-cams de la marque, pensées pour encaisser l'eau et la poussière, la Luna Ultra doit être maniée avec précaution dès que le temps se gâte. Mieux vaudra donc la réserver aux sorties par beau temps ou investir dans une protection complémentaire pour les usages plus exposés, ce qui pourrait en freiner plus d'un parmi les voyageurs et les sportifs.
Sur ce terrain, la nacelle mécanique trois axes de la Luna Ultra, couplée à une stabilisation électronique efficace, gomme les tremblements en toutes circonstances, y compris lors des zooms les plus poussés. Marche rapide, course, montée d'escaliers, prise de vue à vélo : le résultat reste d'une fluidité remarquable dans tous les cas de figure.
La batterie interne de 1550 mAh promet jusqu'à 4 h d’enregistrement, selon Insta360. Dans les faits, et sans surprise, la réalité est un peu moins généreuse : en usage mixte, mêlant 4K et quelques séquences en 8K ou en ralenti, avec écran allumé et suivi actif une bonne partie du temps, on obtient plutôt entre 2 h 30 min et un peu plus de 3 h d'autonomie active. Le power grip du pack créateur permet d'étendre confortablement cette plage sur une journée complète de balade ou de tournage.
Une fois détaché de la Luna Ultra, l'écran fonctionne sur sa propre batterie de 210 mAh, dont l'autonomie plafonne entre 45 et 55 min en usage intensif. Une fois celle-ci épuisée, l'ensemble du système s'arrête purement et simplement, y compris l'enregistrement en cours. Dans le cas d'un long tournage, mieux vaut donc garder l'écran fixé au corps de la caméra, ou surveiller de près son niveau de charge.
Bon point en revanche pour la recharge rapide, compatible USB-C Power Delivery. La Luna Ultra atteint 80 % de charge en une vingtaine de minutes, largement de quoi reprendre son tournage après une courte pause. Le stockage interne de 47 Go, bien qu'inférieur à celui de l'Osmo Pocket 4 P, permet de tenir environ 65 min en 4K/60 i/s sans carte mémoire. La Luna Ultra permet d'ajouter une carte microSD pour ne jamais être pris au dépourvu lors d'un tournage en 8K particulièrement gourmand en espace.
Pour un premier pas, l'Insta360 Luna Ultra frôle le coup de maître. Loin de se contenter de copier la recette de DJI, la marque enrichit intelligemment la formule avec un double objectif pertinent pour varier les plans et un écran-télécommande qui change réellement la manière de filmer certaines scènes. La qualité d'image, la stabilisation et même les performances en basse lumière forcent le respect pour une caméra aussi compacte.
L'Insta360 Luna Ultra n'est cependant pas exempte de défauts avec un autofocus perfectible, une autonomie de l'écran détachable un peu juste, l'absence de certification d'étanchéité et un tarif qui grimpe vite une fois l'appareil équipé des bons accessoires. Reste que pour qui cherche une caméra de poche stabilisée capable de rivaliser avec un vrai appareil photo compact, la Luna Ultra mérite très sérieusement d'être considérée.
La principale concurrente de la Luna Ultra reste évidemment l'Osmo Pocket 4P de DJI, l'unique adversaire direct d'Insta360 sur le terrain des caméras de poche à double objectif. Les deux appareils visent exactement la même cible avec des philosophies proches : capteur 1 pouce principal, téléobjectif secondaire, nacelle trois axes. La Luna Ultra a cependant un argument que DJI ne propose sur aucun de ses modèles avec cet écran détachable qui offre sans surcoût une télécommande. Insta360 marque aussi des points sur l'écosystème logiciel : l'app compagnon, déjà bien rodée sur les autres produits de la marque, s'avère plus aboutie que son équivalent chez DJI avec des modèles de montage automatique convaincants et de vraies possibilités d'édition manuelle pour les utilisateurs plus exigeants. À l'inverse, DJI conserve une avance sur certains points précis, comme le mode time-lapse en mouvement, totalement absent de la Luna Ultra (à l'heure de notre test), ou encore une meilleure maturité générale du firmware, la Luna Ultra étant le tout premier produit de ce type signé Insta360.

articles.title: Lista de electrodomésticos que debes desconectar al salir de vacaciones para pagar menos en la factura
articles.text:
Salir de casa durante varias semanas permite reducir el consumo habitual de electricidad, pero algunos electrodomésticos continúan gastando energía aunque no estén en uso. Por esta razón, desconectar determinados aparatos antes de las vacaciones puede reducir la factura de luz y limitar riesgos dentro del hogar.
La Organización de Consumidores y Usuarios de España (OCU) calcula que, sin contar el ahorro por dejar de utilizar cocina, lavadora u otros aparatos durante la ausencia, desenchufar aparatos puede recortar el recibo en hasta 20 euros.
Los consumos en espera, conocidos como stand-by, representan cerca del 10% de la energía usada en un hogar medio, con un gasto estimado de 7,5 euros mensuales para un consumo anual de 4.500 kWh.
Por qué conviene desconectar la nevera de la red eléctrica
La nevera es uno de los electrodomésticos que más atención requiere antes de un viaje largo. Si la casa permanecerá vacía varios días o semanas y no quedan alimentos que necesiten refrigeración, la OCU aconseja vaciarlo, desenchufarlo y limpiarlo antes de salir.
Después, conviene dejar la puerta abierta para impedir la aparición de humedad, moho y malos olores. Mantener un refrigerador encendido durante un mes puede suponer un gasto de entre 3,5 y 7 euros, según el modelo y su tamaño.
Si es necesario conservar alimentos, se puede elevar ligeramente la temperatura del termostato, porque habrá menos productos en el interior. Algunos modelos combi o de dos puertas permiten apagar la parte del frigorífico y mantener en funcionamiento solo el congelador.
Cuánto consume un termo eléctrico conectado a la red eléctrica
El termo eléctrico debe desconectarse cuando no habrá nadie en casa durante un periodo prolongado. Este aparato mantiene el agua caliente mediante ciclos de calentamiento que se activan aunque no se abra ningún grifo. Dejarlo funcionando puede generar un coste de entre 7 y 10 euros al mes.
Antes de cortar la corriente, los expertos aconsejan cerrar las llaves de paso del agua y utilizar el agua almacenada hasta vaciar el depósito. Esta medida no solo evita un consumo que no tendrá utilidad durante las vacaciones: reduce las consecuencias de una eventual fuga, una rotura o una avería en la instalación.
Qué se debe hacer con la lavadora, el lavavajillas y la secadora
La lavadora, el lavavajillas y la secadora no suelen tener un consumo tan elevado durante la inactividad como un frigorífico o un termo, pero requieren una revisión antes de cerrar la casa.
Deben quedar vacíos para evitar que restos de comida, vajilla usada o prendas húmedas generen olores dentro de los tambores y compartimentos.
Asimismo, es clave secar las gomas y dejar las puertas entreabiertas para que se evapore la humedad acumulada. En el caso del lavavajillas, un paño de cocina puede ayudar a mantener una apertura mínima.
La secadora exige vaciar el depósito de condensación. A la vuelta, la ausencia puede ser una oportunidad para limpiar filtros, revisar el tambor y realizar un ciclo de mantenimiento.
Cuáles son los pequeños aparatos que no deben quedar conectados
Las cafeteras, tostadoras, robots de cocina y otros pequeños electrodomésticos suelen permanecer conectados de forma permanente, aun cuando solo se utilizan unos minutos al día.
Muchos incorporan relojes, luces, pantallas o sistemas de memoria que siguen demandando electricidad mientras están enchufados, incluso si parecen apagados.
La medida a implementar incluye retirar los cargadores de teléfonos, tabletas, aspiradoras y otros dispositivos con batería. La OCU plantea desenchufar todos los aparatos que no necesiten mantenerse encendidos, una práctica que reduce los consumos fantasma y evita que queden conectados aparatos sin supervisión durante la ausencia.
Otro elemento que conviene desconectar es el router. Con ello se elimina su consumo eléctrico durante las vacaciones y se limita la posibilidad de accesos no autorizados a la red WiFi.

The JBL Grip plugs the gap between the smaller Clip and formidable Flip. It's a compact speaker that delivers a big sound, offers impressive protection against dust and water and has some nifty LED lighting on its rear. The Flip 7 is still our top recommendation, but with the Grip currently at the lowest price we have seen for a couple of colour options, it's a great buy.
The Logitech MX Master range have been some of my favourite mice of all time, thanks to the ergonomic design, multiple customisable buttons, and a second scroll wheel for horizontal scrolling (or for flicking through multiple browser tabs). This version is Bluetooth-only, meaning it doesn’t have the Logi Bolt USB dongle and a USB-C charging cable included in the box.
This little pod machine is very popular among TechRadar's Aussie team. We've had past and present staff say how much they love it, and they'd even buy it at full price. With a very compact footprint and plenty of Vertuo pods to choose from, you'll get delicious coffee at just the press of a button.
These AirPods lack active noise cancellation but you still get great audio and personalised spatial audio with dynamic head tracking without having to pay too much. Additionally, a battery life of up to five hours on a single charge and 30 hours with the included carry case will keep you listening for longer. 
Prefer noise cancellation as well? Grab the AirPods 4 with ANC for AU$185 (or 38% off).
Do you remember these, dear reader? These speakers, along with the Harman Kardon Aura, created quite the buzz way back when. The design was fantastic and I personally feel they've withstood the test of time, becoming iconic. In fact, the sound is great too. It's a shame we never got a chance to review the SoundSticks 4, but I've been lusting after them for years! If I had the desktop space, I'd be grabbing these now.
I've just got me this air fryer and its largest glass basket has a 5.7L capacity, so that's a lotta chips! There's another 2.3L borosilicate basket also in the box, so you can just cook a small portion too. And both come with lids, so you can serve in the same basket or cover and store in the fridge. And being glass, it just goes into the dishwasher for a clean.
We've tested the slightly different H60 Hub Ultra here on TechRadar, but not this cheaper, slightly less powerful model. And yet this could be one of the best-value self-emptying stick vacuums to buy right now. For this discounted price you get a lot: up to 170AW of suction, a maximum 80-minute runtime, a free-standing self-emptying dock that has room for attachments, and a green-lit floorhead to spot tiny dirt particles. You don't need much more.
The best entry-level bean-to-cup coffee maker has received a good discount for Prime Day. It's simple to use, taking care of the grinding, tamping and pouring for you. The porta filter will even automatically slide into position for you. Do note there's no milk frothing here, but a matching milk frother is available. Also available in black.
An upgraded version of a watch we proudly awarded five stars, this handy fitness tracker features solar power charging, allowing it to last much longer than the standard model. It's a rugged wrist piece and it's intended for heavy-duty activities.
Deals under AU$100
This discount matches the Blink Video Doorbell System’s last all-time low price during the last Prime Day sale in July. It’s worth noting, though, that many of the features are locked behind the AU$4.95/m Blink Basic or AU$15/m Blink Plus subscription plans, so those costs should be considered if you want video storage, person detection and more. Amazon is also offering a bundle with two Blink Mini 2K+ cameras for AU$48 or 74% off, perfect for a good starter home security system.
This is an excellent budget PC controller and affordable even at full price, but let's not scoff at the AU$13 saving, shall we? Despite its price, there's plenty here to get your game on, including 2.4Ghz wireless connectivity, Bluetooth, a wired option via the Type-C port, and 10 hours of battery life. The build quality isn't the best and there's no audio jack but, for under AU$50, it's a fab buy.
Already quite affordable, this Blink video doorbell can rival anything from the more expensive Ring line, while also offering a long battery life and IP65 weatherproofing. Also included is the Sync Module that you'll need to make everything work, but you will need to take into account that it requires a Blink Subscription Plan if you want all its functions at your fingertips. Note that the 'typical price' listed was the July discount, so this is more than the displayed 7% discount.
This is just the previous Fire TV Stick 4K rebranded to a new name. So if you already have the original, there's no need to upgrade, but for a first-time customer, you get Wi-Fi 6 support and a fast processor so you can get to your favourite streaming content that much quicker. All Fire TV Sticks now get you access to XBox Game Pass, so you don't need a console to play if you already have a subscription.
Read our review for the full scoop, but the Blink Outdoor 4 is an affordable home security camera from Amazon with the ability to last up to two years off batteries. It comes with an easy-to-use app and fairly good camera quality via a 1080p lens, and can store video when paired with a Blink Sync module.
If you're after a really good electric toothbrush that won't cost an arm and a leg (or some teeth), then this is it. It's an entry-level oscillating brush, which means it rotates at fast speeds and may not be ideal for people with sensitive or bleeding gums as that movement can be harsh, but it sure does remove a heck of a lot of plaque and keeps your teeth healthy.
Amazon's Echo Dot it's a great smart speaker with decent sound and Alexa built-in. It also has motion detection and can measure temperature, which is handy if you have a connected thermostat. It is a little long in the tooth now, having released in 2022, but it's a bargain at this price.
Already affordable, these wireless buds have dropped to a record-low price (outdoing the previous one by a single cent). This is excellent value considering we rate them 4.5 stars in our Earfun Air Pro 3 review, and they have active noise cancelling, premium aptX sound quality and 45 hours total play time.
The Lavazza Jolie machines are excellent and affordable alternatives to Nespresso. This Evo model just has a single button for extracting coffee (compared to the Jolie Plus that has programmable buttons), making it oh so simple to use. If you'd like the option to froth milk, you can get a bundle with a frother too.
If you don't enjoy flossing the traditional way, use the power of water instead. Removing plaque using three different water pressure settings, this handy flosser will clean out those hard-to-reach gaps that your toothbrush can't. Plus, it's cordless, meaning you can take it on your travels too. Admittedly these were a lot cheaper in July (just over AU$48), but it was bestseller then, so it would be remiss of me to not include it here again.
Samsung's answer to the AirTag, the SmartTag 2 works with select Samsung phones to help you find mislaid items. It has a built-in hole for easier attachments, up to 700 days of battery life and it's water-resistant. If you're always losing stuff, this is a worthy investment that drops the price of each individual tracker to a mere AU$17.25 apiece.
The Ninja Creami is great and all, but paying almost AU$300 for an ice cream maker is a lot — but this one from Cuisinart costs a fraction of the price and also takes a lot less space too! It's a versatile machine that makes ice cream, slushies, milkshakes, sorbets, and mix-ins to truly earn its space in the kitchen. You can even combine up to three flavours with three included dessert cups.
This food processor's biggest drawcard is its small footprint (30cm tall and 16cm wide), making it great for those with smaller kitchens, but it also has a powerful 650W motor to help blitz foods to slice, grate, chop and knead in seconds. This is the lowest price we've seen for the MultiPro Go, and you can read the full review here.
This drip-style coffee maker lets you wake up to a fresh pot of coffee every morning and it will even keep it warm all morning for those cold days working from home. You can program it to brew at a specific time and even adjust the strength of your brew.
We might be in the middle of winter, but there's no denying some parts of Australia need a good fan year round. This Vornado model creates tornado-like air flow that circulates around the room. Note that this is the smallest model in the range, ideal for bedrooms.
If you're after a compact model that can feed one or two people, this Philips option is great for under a hundred dollary-doos. It's been hovering around the AU$95 mark for a while, so it's quite the best deal, but it's still a discount that's hard to pass up on an air fryer with a staggering 13 preset cooking options.
Headphones & speakers
Offering poised and revealing sound, along with excellent comfort and microphone quality, this saving is one to consider if you've been on the hunt for a quality pair of earbuds. Though noise cancellation and battery life could use some work, we awarded these earbuds a TechRadar Recommends seal of approval in our Technics EAH-AZ80 review.
We gave these stunning earbuds 4.5 stars in our review as they have class-leading audio handling and impeccable sound quality that rivals the best wireless earbuds. With balanced sound, effective ANC and a great battery life, these Sennheiser buds will make any audiophile smile.
Offering “incredible sound”, the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds have all the power and quality you’d expect from a Bose-branded item while providing the benefits of an open-ear form factor. The Immersive sound is excellent, and there’s also up to seven hours of play time and up to 48 hours of standby time. They simply just work and work very well.
Nearly as good as the gen 1 QuietComfort Ultra, the SC misses out on the Immersive Audio mode. There'll also be a little difference in sound quality as they process sound differently, but it's still excellent, as is the ANC performance. You'll also get a soft case for this foldable headphone rather than the hard one for the more expensive set.
The 5th-gen version is out now, but it's our Sennheiser Momentum 4 review that scored a full five stars, where we called these headphones "unbeatable". With active noise-cancellation, 60-hours of battery life and excellent sound quality, there are few pairs that can compete with the Momentum 4.
It's a pity only one colourway is going for this price, but if you don't mind the dusty pink colourway of Sony's latest flagship cans, you'll be in for a treat. Arguably one of the best headphones available today, there's no doubting performance here, with beautifully balanced sound and great ANC.
Clean, detailed sound, full protection against dust and water and all packaged in a gorgeous body, the Bose SoundLink Flex is a Bluetooth speaker you'll want to take with you everywhere you go, and at a pretty good price too.
This visually stunning Bluetooth home speaker is the previous generation (a Studio 5 has been released), but it's still delivers 360º bassy rumbles the Aura series is known for. That's thanks to six outward-firing 40mm drivers with 15W of power each. However, it supports only Bluetooth 4.2 connectivity which, in 2026, can feel unstable compared to the latest standard, but that's hard to fault at this low price (note that the original list price is the previous discounted amount).
This floatable Bluetooth speaker is perfect for the poolside party, with up to 15 hours of playtime and very decent 45m connectivity range. It promises bassy, punchy and yet a clear 360º soundstage.
Vacuum cleaners
This is a very different Dreame R10 to the one we've previously reviewed on TechRadar, but if it performs anything like the light-coloured version that has since been discontinued, then I think this is excellent value. For not a lot of money, this appliance promises up to 45 minutes of runtime and a bendy wand to get under furniture. It even comes with a wall-mount attachment.
With powerful and dynamic suction, plenty of attachments and an auto-empty charging dock, this is arguably the best value non-Dyson cordless vacuum right now. Read our review for the full scoop. Often sold around the AU$750 price point, it as low as AU$438 at the start of this sale, but this is still a great bargain on what I think is the best stick vacuum cleaner in Australia.
This is a fantastic discount on Dyson's most powerful cordless vacuum to date, and what I like even more about it is the quick-release floorhead so you don't have to keep bending to take off or clip it back in again. For your money, you're getting 315AW of suction and a very powerful motor, a new compression dust cup that can hold up to 30 days of compacted dirt, the new anti-tangle FluffyCones floorhead with dust-illuminating light and long runtime too. If you want the latest from the popular brand, this one is it.
This Roborock wet-dry vacuum will leave your hard floors sparkling clean thanks to powerful suction and effective cleaning. It can get up close to edges and the whole body can lay completely flat to help getting underneath tricky to reach places. This price is equal to the lowest we have seen on Amazon and is a great saving on an excellent floor washer – read our review for more info.
Where this Dreame differs from all the others on this page is that if you don't want it to mop (do a vacuum-only run), it can drop its mop pads in the base station by itself. It's also pretty powerful and scored 4 stars in our Dreame X40 Ultra review. It's now two generations old but I'd still recommend it today, especially at this price.
We haven't tested this specific model but we were rather impressed by the Qrevo Curv 2 Pro that's not available in Australia. The Flow version has slightly lower suction (20,000Pa vs 25,000Pa) and uses a roller mop rather than dual pads which I personally prefer. It is a slightly taller bot compared to the Pro model, but if you don't have a lot of low-lying furniture, I would trust this machine based on all other impressive Roborock robovacs my colleagues and I have tested.
Want the latest Dreame tech? Released earlier this year, this robovac packs everything that Dreame models are good at — excellent suction, decent mopping, superb obstacle avoidance, pet-zone cleaning and so much more — into a sleek machine. OK, so it looks like all the others, but c'mon, you can't tell me the white with metallic accents don't fit into any home.
Coffee machines
This compact manual coffee machine can pour up to two espresso shots at once and features a steam wand for cafe-quality milk foaming. There's no built-in grinder, but you either use ground coffee beans or invest in a separate grinder using the cash you save with this deal.
This gorgeous-looking, easy-to-use, bean-to-cup espresso machine is a worthy addition to any coffee lover's kitchen. It's relatively compact, too, and pours delicious espresso with little to no skill involved. Note that this is the non-Evo model, meaning it can't make cold brew. The Evo model is out of stock at the time of writing.
The Breville Bambino Plus is incredibly simple to use, and can take care of most of the coffee making process for you. Grind some beans into the porta filter, insert it into the group head and use the one-touch controls to brew. It also has a hands-free milk texturing system for expertly frothed milk, while ThermoJet technology means the machine is ready to use in seconds. There's very little you need to do to simply enjoy the results — now AU$20 more than what it cost at the start of the sale.
This Philips bean-to-cup machine can make 12 coffee-based drinks, all of which are served perfectly, and can be customised to suit your tastes. We weren't too fond of its milk frothing skills in our LatteGo 4400 Series review, but at this price, I can't recommend it highly enough, even though it was AU$175 cheaper for the first half of the sale thanks to a coupon.
This 3-in-1 coffee machine brews quality espresso, drip coffee and even fast cold brew using its Barista Assist technology, an integrated grinder and weight-based dosing. There's a lot it can do, and it does it very well, with the Cyberspace model offering the best discount.
This at-home espresso machine is perfect for hobbyist baristas and coffee connoisseurs alike and has long held a position on our round-up of the best espresso machines for good reason. This manual coffee machine streamlines the brewing process from beans to latte with its integrated conical burr grinder, steam wand and precise espresso extraction.
It's an expensive machine but we like it so much that it scored 4.5 stars in our De'Longhi Eletta Explore review. Capable of making both hot and cold coffee brews, this bean-to-cup machine produces delicious results, although it's not without its quirks. Our reviewer thought its water tank design was a little annoying and wasn't too thrilled with the two-carafe milk system, but if those aren't going to be issues for you, this could be a good investment.
Air fryers
This big air fryer has multiple accessories to keep clean, but there's no denying this Sunbeam unit is a fantastic addition to any kitchen. It's capable of cooking in separate zones, complete with separate trays to maximise the space or one huge 11.4L zone. Food is roasted to perfection, whether it's a full chicken or small portions of fries or vegetables.
Securing a spot on our list of the best air fryers, our reviewer said this innovative model from Ninja was the "air fryer of my dreams". It takes a familiar double drawer design, but stacks them on top of each other, resulting in a smaller footprint. Performance is exemplary, but just make sure the food you put in isn't that big, as the drawers themselves are on the smaller side at 4.75L each.
We haven't tested Philips' dual basket air fryer, but considering how much we've loved the brand's other kitchen appliances, it's hard to not make a mention of this offer. This 9L air fryer has drawers of different sizes, which makes it easy to cook a main and a side together, and promises to sync cooking times if needed.
This compact air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glassware containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate means they can also withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy, and it's safer to use than any non-stick basket. The Crispi also comes with two removable crisping grates and two snap-on container lids for easy food-storage post-feast.
Ever cooked with steam in an air fryer? Now you can with this Philips two-drawer air fryer. In my Philips 5000 Series Dual Basket XXL Air Fryer Steam review, I said that it cooks everything really well, but there are some caveats to keep in mind when it comes to the use of steam. Still, it's absolutely worth the investment if you want to upgrade from an old air fryer and you have the space for it.
OK, hear me out about why this is being grouped with the air fryers: because this countertop oven can air fryer as one of its many functions. And like other air fryers it can also grill, roast and dehydrate. What it can do that standard air fryers can't is also bake like a convection fan-forced oven, which can be very handy indeed. Oh, it can steam too. If this ain't good value as a kitchen upgrade, I dunno what is, but you will need the space for it on your counter.
Phones & tablets
We named the Nothing Phone (4a) the best overall cheap phone for its mix of good mid-range specs, unique design, clean Android UI and low price. Its cameras can be better and there's no wireless charging here, but it's to be expected for a phone at this price point.
It looks like an iPhone and can rival Apple's performance too, thanks to a powerful chipset under the hood. In fact, our tester was quite impressed with this phone in our Xiaomi 17T review, with the biggest issue being bloatware. If that doesn't bother you, we gave this one four stars.
Costing less than Apple’s budget phone — the AU$1,149 iPhone 17e — the base model Samsung Galaxy S26 is a true flagship device with three camera lenses, 12GB of RAM and the full Galaxy AI suite. We've seen this dip below AU$1,000 recently, but this price is still a bargain given how much more expensive flagship phones are these days. Amazon has the Black, Cobalt Violet, Sky Blue and White colours available for this price, and you can also trade in an old phone for more savings.
The latest in Samsung's well-received budget tablet range, the A11 picks up where the A9 left off, and at the same price too. This is the base model, with just Wi-Fi connectivity and 128GB of storage, but you can expand that easily to up to 2TB via a microSD card. If you need an Android tablet for daily use like browsing, watching videos and maybe playing a few games, this one's well worth considering, although it has been available for less than AU$300 previously.
With more storage than the standard Paperwhite, a brighter screen and wireless charging, the Paperwhite Signature Edition is arguably better value than the base model above if you think you'll make full use of the storage and its wireless charging capabilities. If not, you're better off going with the standard Paperwhite, although its meagre discount is rather disappointing.
The Kindle Colorsoft is one of the best ereaders with a colour display, even offering a feature to make the hues more vivid. While I wouldn't recommend at full price, this discount makes it a little easier on the pocket for the 32GB version that also has wireless charging.
Summer must-haves
SodaStream is a leading name in sparkling water makers and the Art is an entry-level model that uses a retro-inspired pull lever to add CO2 to water rather than the usual button on models like the SodaStream Terra. This sparkling water maker will also get you a bottle and a gas cylinder to start, and you can purchase flavourings and get the cylinder replaced or refilled easily enough.
Not only will you be able to make single-serve smoothies with this blender, it will also let you prepare larger batches, thanks two two jars. Its headline act, however, is the alert that you'll get if it needs a little extra liquid for the smoothest results. And it's a heck of a lot cheaper than the more popular Ninja BlendBoss, which is down to AU$141.55 in different colour options.
A welcome saving on Breville's answer to the SodaStream. Not only can you use the InFizz Fusion to carbonate water, but you can fizz any liquid you can think of — other than hot beverages of course. This nifty machine is sure to be a hit during at-home cocktail nights.
It's got a cult-like following and two members of our own staff are massive fans. If you love your chilled desserts – ice creams, gelatos, smoothies – but want to control your calorie intake, you really should consider getting the Ninja Creami. This Deluxe edition gets you three containers, which is great value at this price, although it was over AU$50 cheaper in July.
The Ninja Slushi lets you skip the ice and still enjoy perfectly smooth icy drinks with very little effort. Whether you're craving a frappe, smoothie, or even a cheeky spiked slushi, its multiple drink modes have you covered. Check out our Ninja Slushi review for the full rundown.
This is one of the better deals we have seen for the Creami lately. Read our review for more info, but you can think of it as the Creami’s upgraded sibling. It handles everything the original model does, then goes further with a built-in soft-serve unit featuring six dedicated programs.
When space is a premium and you only require cooling in a focused area, then a tower fan might be for you. This one from Philips is only 23.8cm deep and wide to fit a small space like a corner or a narrow hallway, while also standing 109.5cm tall to provide more cooling.
This fan can be used either at home, plugged in, or on the go with its built-in battery that’s rated for up to 12 hours of continuous operation. The water droplets from the misting function are ultra-fine and come from an integrated tank, so the feature also works while on the go. A built-in handle and lightweight 1.76kg body also make the FlexBreeze HydroGo easy to transport and move around.
This bladeless fan may be the priciest in this list, but this discount still makes the Shark TurboBlade Ultra a more affordable option than Dyson’s offerings. The fan can either be set horizontally to cover a wider area or vertically for more focused cooling. It comes with 10 speed options and different noise levels to suit whatever your cooling needs are.
This portable aircon can rapidly cool down a space of up to 20sqm while also running relatively quietly for as low as 64db. We haven't reviewed this yet, but it has dozens of 5-star user reviews for its ease of installation and effectiveness.
This portable aircon also doubles as a dehumidifier and can cool down a room of up to 30sqm, while also running at 64db during low-speed mode. TechRadar hasn't reviewed this yet, but it has a handful of 5-star user reviews praising its portability and performance.
Personal care
Fitted with a flexible head, this shaver is designed to glide against the shape of your face, while onboard sensors will allow it to adapt the cutting power to your beard's length. Speaking of which, it's got 5 length settings to suit different needs and it holds its own while in the shower too.
This premium electric shaver is going for such a good price right now that I think it would make an excellent Christmas gift for the deserving man. With sensors to analyse facial hair 160x times a second, it promises precise strokes for the perfect, close shave without the hefty price tag.
The Dreame Gleame hair dryer is an even more affordable alternative to the bigger brands. Its motor spins at a mighty fast 110,000 RPM for fast airflow and quick drying, plus built-in ion technology results in smooth, shiny hair. Not to mention, the slim, lightweight build make it comfortable to hold.
Much like Dyson's Airstrait but more versatile thanks to different attachments, this is a hair styler that can dry and style at the same time. It's not quite perfect — Shark improved on it with the newer SilkiPro — but this discount is still hard to pass up for a styler that can save you time and offer you different coiffures each day of the week.
If you didn't know what a 'sonic' brush is, it's quieter and gentler than an oscillating electric toothbrush (like Oral-B). The DiamondClean 9000 has 4 cleaning modes, and one of them gets you 3 intensities. This value pack gets you a his-and-hers version, plus the glass is actually the charger.
Home entertainment & Hi-Fi
The latest version of LG's moveable, portable TV can be a useful addition to your home. Not only will it stream all your fave services, but you can use it a work monitor or home hub with calendars, chore lists, shopping lists, whatever you want. It has just 4 hours of battery life though, and a resolution of 1440p, but our tester was quite taken by in our LG StanByMe 2 review.
Prefer 4K resolution with Dolby Vision? The LG StanByMe 2 Max is also discounted but only by 8%.
The Amazon Fire TV Cube combines all the benefits of a streaming device with Alexa support. It works as a smart speaker so you can control your smart home devices with it, but it also provides access to every streaming app you can think of. Throw in Dolby Vision, HDR, and Dolby Atmos, and it’s everything you could want. So why not grab a streaming device that's also a smart speaker?
This budget-friendly 2.1 soundbar is ideal for anyone looking to upgrade their TV or computer audio without spending much money. We were pleasantly surprised by how it performed in our Creative Stage Pro review, finding it delivered impressive bass and excellent volume. Given its size and price, expectations should be tempered, but for a cost-effective audio upgrade, it's ace.
In our Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar review, we said this soundbar rivals the Sonos Arc, which is the best Sonos soundbar we've tried. The Smart Ultra is compact, beautifully built, and offers plenty of control options to go with its wide, detailed sound.
This Sony Bluetooth turntable is as fuss-free as they come with regard to setup and getting your favourite vinyl records spinning. Whether you're playing via wired or wireless speakers, it delivers a delightfully musical sound that will satisfy vinyl beginners or those looking for a more hands-off approach. Please note that this is a bigger discount than the 14% Amazon is displaying as the listed 'typical price' was the previous discounted price.
Arguably one of the most iconic turntables available right now, the Sound Burger is lightweight, works wirelessly with up to 12 hours of playtime, has Bluetooth connectivity and is easy to use. It's a fabulous entry into the world of vinyl at a fantastic price.
Fitness trackers & smartwatches
We called it "nearly the perfect fitness tracker" in our Oura Ring 4 review, praising the design, ease-of-use, long-lasting battery and detailed health information it offers. This fascinating bit of tech hasn't been cheaper and, even though you need a subscription, it can be well worth it for the comprehensive health data you can get. Note that prices vary depending on colour and size, but most are discounted.
The 'S' in the name stands for 'small', meaning this specific Garmin was made for petite wrists and features a 42mm vibrant OLED display. You also get Multiband GPS, an intuitive menu navigation, excellent battery life, plenty of Garmin fitness features... and, oh, did I mention the OLED display?
Dash cams
Holding a spot on our list of the best dash cams, the Vantrue E1 is super compact, yet is capable of recording clear, detailed footage day and night. A comprehensive mobile, PC and Mac app allows for easy footage transfers and built-in GPS ensures you know exactly where any incidents take place.
We call this an "all-round surveillance solution" in our 70mai Dash Cam A510 review, due to it including both front-facing and rear-facing cameras in the box. They're quality cameras, too, recording 2.7K footage from the front and 1080p at the back, complete with wide fields of view. Built-in GPS, 360º rotation for in-car recording and easy install only add to its appeal.
Gaming hardware
This deal offers you a significant saving on the new, higher price on Meta's best 'affordable' headset, and a close second to its best ever headset according to our resident VR headset tester. In fact, he thinks it's the second-best headset anyone can buy from any brand, and it's only a more tempting offer thanks to this limited-time deal.
Please don't confuse this with the ROG Xbox Ally X, which has more powerful specs. This is the cheaper sibling that now costs AU$10 more than its July Prime Day price. However, given the price hikes across the board on all game consoles, this seems like a tempting buy right now. This was AU$799 during Amazon's Mid-Year Sale in early June, but it would be remiss of me to not list this discount here.
This handheld gaming PC has been cheaper before, dropping to the AU$899 mark but, then again, nothing really comes cheap these days. Importantly, though, this is a great performer, with a vivid 8-inch display and 144Hz refresh rate for smooth gameplay. It's also rather nice looking and comfortable in the hand.
Sure, it's a wired controller, but this gamepad is simple to use and durable, with drift-free hall effect analog sticks. In fact, the base of the sticks also have RGB, which is fantastic at this price. Being wired, however, means this isn't ideal for couch play, but if you're a PC gamer at your desk, it'll do wonderfully well.
[Shipped and sold by Amazon UK]
While we've not reviewed this 75% mechanical gaming keyboard ourselves, reviews from other reputable sources across the web are largely glowing, praising its construction quality, performance and low price. This Prime Big Deal Days discount brings the cost to a new all-time Aussie low — though note that it's only available at this price in black. Other colourways start from AU$94.23.
If you prefer your gaming keyboards with a numpad, this 96% option is a great alternative to the Epomaker F75 above. It's likewise accrued positive reviews (both professional and from users) and even includes a customisable colour LCD display. This price is just AU$1 more than its all-time Australian low. Also available with a similar discount in blue/white and pink colourways.
Boasting a 12,000dpi 'Hero' sensor, as well as 6 programmable buttons, a 250-hour battery and onboard memory for your settings, the Logitech G305 Lightspeed Wireless Gaming Mouse is ideal for competitive play. Want to know more? Check out our review, but not that only the blue and lilac colourways get the best discount.
One of the best gaming mice available right now, the Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2 Dex is an exceptionally lightweight and capable device, with a long-lasting battery life, five programmable buttons and a 32K DPI sensor.
A nice 30% off deal on a 27-inch OLED gaming monitor, bringing it down to the lowest price we have seen on Amazon. It features a 180Hz panel capable of a 4K resolution. We awarded four and a half stars to this screen in our Alienware 27 AW2725Q review, and were impressed with its sharp visuals and HDR performance.
This OLED monitor comes with a gigantic 34.2-inch curved screen that boasts a 240Hz refresh rate and a lightning fast 0.03ms response time. It’s capable of producing gorgeous darkness with DisplayHDR TrueBlack 400 certification, and offers a 3440 x 1440 resolution.
PC peripherals
This ergonomic vertical mouse is perfect for small hands and it encourages better posture, thus reducing aches along the wrist, shoulder and shoulder blade. I use it myself (I have the white colourway) and can't recommend it highly enough, even at full price.
A 100Hz-refresh-rate monitor for just AU$100? Sign me up! This display from Lenovo may be a bit small at under 24 inches with a 1080p resolution, but it uses IPS technology for sharp image quality. This is price is the lowest we've seen this monitor go on Amazon.
It might sound like coffee but Espresso makes some of the best portable displays on the market and this Lite version of a 15-inch add-on is relatively affordable compared to the brand's other offerings even at full price. With a simple USB-C connection, it's ready to go out of the box with 400 nits of peak brightness in 1080p resolution. It's also relatively light and compact, in case you need to travel with it.
The MX Keys S Combo is an excellent desk upgrade if you want a premium keyboard and mouse without paying anywhere near the usual bundle price. It combines the backlit MX Keys S with the quiet, ergonomic MX Master 3S, plus a palm rest, and both can switch between up to three devices.
I've used the T5 previously and currently use the 2TB T7 Shield, and while it's tempting to upgrade, it's still plenty fast. So just imagine how good the upgraded portable SSD will be for you if you're looking for a safe and reliable backup solution for all your files. The 1TB T9 has apparently been as cheap as AU$190 before, but that was way back in 2024. It's since hovered around this price.
In our 4-star review from last year, we praised this speedy tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router for its combination of advanced hardware and flexible OS (the excellent OpenWRT) at an impressively affordable price. It's only weak spot? It lacks mesh capabilities. GL.iNet has since released a beta firmware that aims to rectify that, but we still think it's best suited to use as a single router in an apartment or smaller home. This deal is just a couple of dollars shy of its previous Australian low.
Google's Wi-Fi 6e capable mesh system is worth considering for big homes, although we've seen discounts that make this 3-pack cheaper than half price. You can position each unit around your home to create an even blanket of Wi-Fi, cracking down on dead spots.
If you aren't keen on the Google mesh Wi-Fi system listed above, consider Amazon's own Eero 6+ three-pack instead. You should read our full review to get the complete picture, but we gave the Eero 6+ 4 stars, and noted that the Wi-Fi performance was excellent, the pricing is good and it's easy to use.
The latest eero Wi-Fi 7 mesh router is down to the lowest price we have seen on Amazon. We don't have a review yet, but our friends over at Tom's Guide rated it 4-stars. It's a Wi-Fi 7 model designed for high-speed wireless and wired networks and includes dual 5GbE ports.
Smart home
I've tried a fair few smart home devices in my time but not the Meross smart plugs. Still, something has got to be said about the 4.6-star rating on Amazon with some very happy customers saying it's a great product. Smart plugs are a great way to turn any gadget at home into a smart one, including lamps and kettles. Where the Meross stands out from other affordable offerings is by also featuring an energy monitor — a great way to keep tabs on your usage and save money on power bills.
This 8-inch smart display will need to be wall-mounted and it gives you control of thousands of smart home devices that work over Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and other connectivity standards like Zigbee, Matter and Thread. You can stream video, even security footage, start routines, add widgets and a heck of a lot more you can't with a regular Echo Show — now at its lowest price yet.
This smart alarm clock combines all the best Alexa features and a digital clock, making it all the easier to wake up with a pep in your step. It was surprising to see it didn't get a discount in the last few Amazon sales, so this 20% off is welcome, but it has been available for AU$99 previously.
As of October last year, the RRP for this floor lamp was just AU$149, something that made me give it a high value score on my Nanoleaf Smart Multicolor Floor Lamp review. Now, though, the RRP is AU$169.99 – blame inflation, I suppose — but Amazon is still sticking with the original price. What that means is this is a bigger discount than it first appears. Either way, this is one of the cheapest smart lamps you can get, one that does exactly what it promises on the tin. I have one in my bedroom and, although it's not bright, it creates lovely wall-washing effects.
The Philip Hue Play bar light will amplify your lounge room setup. And given the two-pack makes more economical sense to pick up, you place one on either side of your telly to create some stunning backlighting. While you will need a Hue Hub (sold separately) if you want to sync or screen mirror, the Play can still create quite the ambience on movie nights.
It's been a while since I've seen a good Nanoleaf Shapes discount on Amazon, so I'm stoked to find this. It will make a lovely Christmas gift or you can use it to create spooky Halloween effects this month, the possibilities are endless if you want to get creative. I'm not a great fan of the Nanoleaf app itself but I can't fault the lights.
I much prefer this design of the newest Echo Show 8 smart display, now powered by a AZ3 Pro chip for better performance and 15% more screen real estate than previous generations. It's a much better smart hub now, with Alexa at your beck and call (and fingertips).
LIVE: Latest Updates
Do you need to spend hundreds on a Lego set?
Lego has always been a relatively pricey purchase as far as toys go, but the company has been making more and more sets close to and over AU$1,000, like the 7,541-piece Lego Star Wars Millennium Falcon 75192 and the 9,023-piece Lego Star Wars Death Star 75419.
This has been a deliberate move into the luxury toy category by Lego, targeting the so-called Adult Fans of Lego (AFOL) with its own dedicated division. These sets range from licenced IP-based sets like the Star Wars ones above to recreations of the Titanic and the Eiffel Tower (both have more than 9,000 pieces and cost AU$999.99 RRP).
Apart from the extra cost incurred by licencing fees for some sets, Lego also justifies the premium price with its bricks being manufactured with a tolerance of 0.005mm to ensure that every single brick it made from as early as 1960 will still snap in perfectly onto a newly made brick today. The bricks are also made with high-quality ABS plastic, and the expensive steel moulds to make the bricks have to be replaced frequently — both contributing to the premium pricing.
Lego's Technic line also has some high-end sets that include motors and even Bluetooth connectivity to allow controlling the built set through a smartphone app. The now-retired AU$1,049.99 Lego Liebherr Crawler Crane features multiple motors and Bluetooth hubs — which were more expensive than the plastic bricks themselves.
Should you buy these sets? If you have cash to spend, sure — but you'll also need enough room to display them once they're assembled, because these can get huge. The Lego Star Wars Millennium Falcon I mentioned above is 83cm long and 60cm wide, while the Eiffel Tower set is almost as tall as an adolescent child at 149cm!
On the other hand, Lego's new Smart Play sets are even more interactive, offering a sound-and-light show thanks to a 'smart brick' — and these sets aren't all that expensive.
Long story short, if you love Lego and have the cash, indulge yourself. I most definitely do!
Please flip out on this deal
Besides a capable pair of headphones, I'd argue the other audio essential for the discerning music listener is a Bluetooth speaker, and few are as talented at the JBL Flip 6, even though the Flip 7 has now succeeded it.
It's built tough to survive knocks and bumps, while an IP67-rating means it's protected against dust and water. It's a talented performer across the entire frequency range, although it's the bass department we have to give particular praise to. This thing can go real low, thanks to dual passive radiators, while a separate tweeter takes care of the mids and highs. It has no issue filling a room either, especially if you pair it with multiple other Flip 6s (you can connect up to 100 if you're so inclined).
And while we are definitely fans of the Flip 7 here at TechRadar, why would you pay upwards of AU$150 for the latter when the Flip 6 is ultimately quite similar... and a lot cheaper with this deal?
JBL Flip 6: AU$169.95 AU$99.95
Apple to the Max: part 2
If you've had your eye on Apple's latest-release over-ear headphones, you're in luck as this Amazon sale has one colourway that's at the receiving end of a small discount — there's AU$100 off only the Starlight model of the Apple AirPods Max 2.
Not the best price as some colours were down to AU$799 in July, but then I really wasn't expecting any discount on these cans. So can't really complain.
I don't necessarily want the cans as I already use the AirPods Pro 3, but some of you who prefer the larger set would love the improvements the H2 chip brings to the Max 2. They will work with the iPhone 15 or newer Apple handsets and, as our AirPods Max 2 review says, they're one of the best headphones available today, albeit at a hefty price.
Among the new features these headphones bring are live translate, advanced call screening, gesture control, conversational awareness, and adaptive audio. Pair all of these with a stunning high-end design, class-leading noise cancellation, and fantastic audio quality, and the AirPods Max 2 are definitely worth considering.
Apple AirPods Max 2: AU$999 now AU$899
Go with this compact stand mixer
KitchenAid's popular stand mixers might be the staple in most kitchens, but not everyone has the space — or money — for them. Enter the Kenwood Go range, which has a 4L stand mixer with a small footprint.
Sure, you won't be able to beat or knead large batches of cake batter or bread dough, but it still serves a purpose. I should know, I have one (the Clay Red) and it's not just adorable, but very useful in my tiny one-bedroom apartment in Sydney where space is at a premium.
Even at full price (AU$399) it's a fraction of the price a KitchenAid would cost you, but there's AU$100 off right now on all three colours.
Kenwood Go stand mixer: AU$399 now AU$299
Even at full price, these are something
Nothing has made some of our favourite headphones and earbuds in the last couple of years, nearly every one of them well received by our audio experts, and the CMF sub-brand brings in the budget goods that don't really make too many compromises.
Take the CMF by Nothing Buds Pro 2 wireless buds: even at full price, they cost under a hundred dollary-doos! And while they got a small 5% discount in July, they've been neglected this time round. Yet they're packed full of value and lovely sound.
If you want some high-quality earbuds for cheap that rival the audio performance and noise cancellation of the AirPods, but at a much — MUCH — lower price, these are it. And in some nice colours too.
CMF by Nothing Buds Pro 2: AU$95
What is Alexa+ and is it worth it?
I'm sure by now we're all familiar with Alexa, Amazon's voice assistant, even though we may not have used it if we're more dependent on Google Assistant/Gemini or Siri.
Alexa+ is just a smarter, more conversational version of the original — or, to use technical jargon, it's a generative AI model. While it can do everything the original Alexa could, it does more than answer specific questions or perform set tasks. It can remember your personal information and can take context into account, which is how it becomes more conversational when you ask it to do something for you.
The result is a more personalised assistant that delivers better outcomes and learns from your behaviour in order to make more relevant suggestions.
Alexa+ is available on nearly all the current Echo devices and is a free add-on for Prime members, but a subscription costs AU$29.99 a month for everyone else. Another reason to hold on to the AU$9.99p/m Prime subscription, isn't it?
Whether Alexa+ is worth the upgrade is up to you and which AI assistant you prefer. With Gemini just as popular, there's competition and, much like its counterparts, Alexa+ is better at understanding you and one of the reasons for that is because you can feed it information which it will retain. You can tell it what you like and don’t like, share facts and key dates such as birthdays and the types of food you enjoy. You can also share photos, messages, emails, documents and calendar events, and get Alexa+ to draw upon the information for use in its responses and suggestions.
Alexa, is there a cheap Echo in here?
Yup, Christmas is coming and if you're keen on finding a lovely tech gift that won't cost the earth, then consider the Amazon Echo Dot.
Yes, it's an older model, but that's also why it's cheap and, given the Echo Pop has been discontinued and the Echo Spot isn't quite as affordable as I had hoped this Prime Day, this Echo Dot will do you just fine for a bare-bones, entry-level smart speaker.
In fact, it will even support Alexa+ which is free for Prime members.
It was AU$43 in July, so this isn't the best price, but it's still affordable.
Amazon Echo Dot (5th gen): AU$99 now AU$59
Let's talk toast
There are toasters and there are toasters, none need to cost as much as AU$400, but then again, maybe they do.
I'm not saying I can justify the high asking price of the Breville Eye Q, but damn, it makes fabulous toast, just how I like it. It uses optic sensors to determine the doneness of the bread based on the colour (and that's chosen by the user of course) rather than heat sensors, and it has a specific mode for artisanal breads too. Whether you like it well browned or just lightly toasted, the Breville Eye Q can do it just right every time.
Well, at least it won't cost you AU$400 to get perfect toast every morning thanks to this discount.
Breville Eye Q (2-slice; Noir Black): AU$419 now AU$299
Wake up and smell the coffee
The Nespresso Vertuo Pop is the famed coffee maker's smallest machine, yet it doesn't scrimp on features. Being part of the Vertuo lineup, it uses a wider range of pods that can brew a range of coffee sizes, from single espresso all the way up to a full mug.
This machine has been one of our faves here at TechRadar ever since it launched in 2023, with a couple of my colleagues using it themselves at home and none of any complaints. It works just as you'd expect and couldn't be simpler. All you need to do is pop a pod in and press a button, the machine takes care of the rest — it's that easy.
The AU$199 RRP is already good value in my opinion, but a discount sees the compact pod machine drop to under AU$100 a... pop. Not the cheapest price, admittedly (which was AU$88), but not too far away.
Nespresso Vertuo Pop: AU$229 now AU$92.15
Read all about it: New Kindle ereaders up for pre-order
If you haven't heard yet, Amazon has just announced a brand-new lineup of Kindle ereaders, 2026 edition. These include two entry-level Kindles (the usual 16GB storage and, now a 32GB model as well in different colours), new Paperwhite and Colorsoft, with the latter two also getting new Signature Editions as well.
They were announced at 11pm AEST on Thursday, October 1 and they're up for pre-order if you want to upgrade your summer reading experience. All new Kindles start shipping November 11, but I don't think we should expect to see any of them discounted during Black Friday.
Over 9,000 Aussie shoppers have joined me so far on my deal-hunting expedition on Amazon, and I'm very grateful for your company — hopefully I've been able to help you not just find tech you need or like, but also save you some cash in the bargain.
I'm still at it, of course, as there are some new offers still popping up, or perhaps I just missed them earlier on. You have until midnight tonight (Eastern time) to get your shopping sorted but, if you miss out, it's a good thing that Black Friday sales aren't too far away now.

articles.title: Vous utilisez Gemini ? Mauvaise nouvelle : Google réserve désormais ses meilleurs modèles à ceux qui paient le prix cher
articles.text:
Vous utilisez Gemini ? Mauvaise nouvelle : Google réserve désormais ses meilleurs modèles à ceux qui paient le prix cher
Dès le 9 octobre, les comptes Gemini sans abonnement seront cantonnés à Flash-Lite, le modèle le plus léger de la gamme. La formule AI Plus à 4,99 € perd elle aussi le modèle Pro, désormais réservé aux forfaits à 21,99 € et au-delà.
L'annonce tient dans une page d'aide de Google, mise à jour cette semaine et repérée le 3 octobre par 9to5Google. Le texte décrit une nouvelle répartition des modèles dans l'application Gemini pour les comptes personnels. Moins de cinq mois après l'instauration de quotas calculés selon la puissance consommée, la gratuité rétrécit encore d'un cran.
Gemini gratuit limité à Flash-Lite : ce qui change le 9 octobre
Le tableau publié par Google tient en trois colonnes : Flash-Lite, Flash et Pro. Sans forfait, seule la première reste ouverte. Aujourd'hui encore, la page française des abonnements promet aux comptes gratuits un accès à 3.6 Flash et un "accès variable" à 3.1 Pro. Ces deux portes se ferment.
Les abonnés AI Plus conservent Flash-Lite et Flash, et voient Pro leur échapper. Google leur annonce un courriel précisant la date d'application. Pour retrouver le modèle le plus capable, il faudra donc passer à AI Pro, facturé 21,99 € par mois en France, ou à AI Ultra, proposé à partir de 99,99 €.
Deep Think arrive dans Google AI Pro, avec des quotas toujours comptés
La formule AI Pro reçoit une compensation de taille : Deep Think, l'option de raisonnement parallèle la plus poussée de Gemini, que la grille tarifaire range encore parmi les avant-premières d'AI Ultra.
Autre nouveauté : trois niveaux d'effort (faible, moyen, élevé) pour chaque modèle disponible. Monter d'un cran promet des réponses plus fouillées. Google prévient toutefois que ce réglage "utilisera aussi une plus grande part de votre limite".
Car les quotas demeurent. Depuis le 17 mai, ils se rechargent toutes les cinq heures jusqu'à épuisement d'un plafond hebdomadaire. AI Plus double la limite standard, AI Pro la quadruple.
Une inconnue subsiste : Gemini 4 Argon, annoncé le 30 septembre et promis d'abord aux abonnés AI Ultra et aux clients payants de l'API. Google garde le silence sur la catégorie qui l'accueillera dans l'application. Les adeptes du gratuit, eux, garderont un assistant amputé de sa meilleure matière grise.
